text: Riders operate cycles via pedal-powered machines, including bicycles and tricycles, whether moving over flat terrain or air-filled wheels constructed from rubber. Iron components serve as brakes, featuring brake pads mounted within the hub located at the rear assembly of the vehicle. Upon pedaling, these pads shift vertically to press against the tire rim. Control is managed through a handlebar-mounted controller that connects to the bicycle's rear section. This control unit generally incorporates dual pedals positioned on opposite sides of the frame.
